source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Seeing the kerning studies side by side, Option 2 (Balanced Flow) is definitely the direction I'm most drawn to. It reads as one cohesive word while still maintaining the elegance and airiness we've been building.

Before moving into the material treatments, I'd like to revisit the terminal shared by the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

We spent a great deal of time refining the Hero V before the rest of the alphabet existed. At that stage, it needed to carry much more of the identity on its own. Now that the entire wordmark has come together, I don't think it needs to feel quite as decorative or expressive.

The feeling I'm after is precision, confidence, and quiet elevation. I'd love to explore a terminal that feels more architectural and intentional—a clean, controlled upward release rather than a flourish.

I'm attaching two references that begin to communicate the character I'm describing. I'm not looking to copy either one exactly, but I am drawn to the cleaner transition and the more restrained sense of elevation.

I don't want to change the established slope or structure of the Hero V and second V. Instead, I'd love to see a few interpretations that maintain the same geometry while refining the terminal consistently across the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

Thank you!

missing_event_candidates.decision_note: The client postpones further material-treatment work until the shared terminal is refined.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

After reviewing the latest presentation, I have decided to end the project. The Hero V and second V do not maintain the locked hierarchy and geometry we had established in any of these examples, despite explicit instructions.

At this stage, continuing would require reopening and reconstructing decisions that had already been resolved. I do not believe another revision cycle would be the best use of either of our time.

Please do not make any further design revisions. Please send me all editable working files created throughout the project, including the original vector/source files, presentation boards, and exported artwork in their current state.

Thank you for the time and work you have invested in the project. I wish you the best moving forward.

Brittany

missing_event_candidates.decision_note: Ending the project and prohibiting further revisions removes the outstanding material-treatment requirement.
